name: vim file
description: Open one or more files in Vim from the shell.

flags.description: Open with the cursor on line N
Open at the first match of a pattern
Diff mode: compare 2-4 files side by side
Open files in vertical / horizontal splits
Open each file in a tab

examples.description: Open a file
Jump straight to line 120
Diff two files (]c / [c jump between changes)
Open changed files in tabs

notes: `vimdiff a b` is the same as `vim -d a b`. Inside Vim, `:e path` opens another file.

name: :w / :q / :wq / :q! / :x / ZZ
description: Save and quit commands.

examples.description: Save
Save and quit (:x or ZZ also save, but only write if there are changes)
Quit and discard unsaved changes (ZQ does the same)
Save all buffers (:qa quits all, :wqa saves and quits all)
Save a file you opened without root permissions (classic Vim; may not work in Neovim)

notes: WARNING: :q! and ZQ discard all unsaved changes in the buffer.
`:w newname.txt` saves a copy under a new name; `:saveas` switches to it.

name: i / a / o / v / Esc
description: Switch between Normal, Insert, Visual, and Command-line modes.

examples.description: Insert before the cursor (I = start of line)
Append after the cursor (A = end of line)
Open a new line below (O = above) and insert
Return to Normal mode (Ctrl-[ also works)
Enter Command-line mode for Ex commands

notes: Normal mode is home: always press Esc before typing commands. R enters Replace mode.

name: w / b / e
description: Move forward to the next word start, back to the previous word start, or to the word end.

examples.description: Next word start (W uses whitespace-separated WORDs)
Previous word start (B for WORDs)
End of word (E for WORDs; ge goes to the previous word end)
Move forward three words (counts work with most motions)

name: 0 / ^ / $ / f / t
description: Move within the current line.

examples.description: Start of line
First non-blank character
End of line
Jump to the next comma on the line (t, stops before it; ; and , repeat)

name: gg / G / % / :N
description: Jump around the file: top, bottom, a line number, or a matching bracket.

examples.description: First line
Last line (42G goes to line 42)
Go to line 42
Jump to the matching (), [], or {}
Scroll half a page down / up
Jump back / forward through the jump list

name: dd / x / D
description: Delete (cut) lines or characters into a register.

examples.description: Delete the current line (3dd deletes three)
Delete the character under the cursor
Delete to end of line
Delete to the next word (any operator + motion works: d}, dG, dgg)

notes: Deleted text goes into the unnamed register, so dd then p moves a line.

name: yy / p / P
description: Copy (yank) text and paste (put) it.

examples.description: Yank the current line (5yy yanks five)
Put after the cursor / below the line
Put before the cursor / above the line
Yank the word under the cursor

name: ciw / cw / cc / ci"
description: Change text: delete it and enter Insert mode in one step.

examples.description: Change the word under the cursor
Change everything inside the quotes (also ci(, ci{, cit for HTML tags)
Change the whole line
Change to end of line

notes: The i/a text objects (inner/around) work with any operator: daw, yi(, va{.

name: u / Ctrl-r
description: Undo and redo changes.

examples.description: Undo the last change
Redo
Restore the buffer to how it was 5 minutes ago (:later to go forward)

notes: Enable `:set undofile` to keep undo history after closing a file.

description: Repeat the last change.

examples.description: Repeat the last edit at the cursor
Change a word, jump to the next search match, and repeat the change

name: /pattern / n / N / *
description: Search forward or backward and step through matches.

examples.description: Search forward (?TODO searches backward)
Next / previous match
Search for the word under the cursor (# searches backward)
Clear search highlighting

notes: Add \c to make a search case-insensitive (/todo\c), or use `:set ignorecase smartcase`.

name: :%s/old/new/g
description: Find and replace text with the substitute command.

examples.description: Replace all occurrences in the file
Replace with confirmation for each match
Replace the first match on the current line only
Comment out the visually selected lines
Strip trailing whitespace (e suppresses 'not found' errors)

notes: % means every line; omit it for the current line or give a range like :10,20s/a/b/g. Use a different delimiter for paths: :%s#/usr/local#/opt#g.

name: :g/pattern/d
description: Run an Ex command on every line matching a pattern.

examples.description: Delete all lines containing DEBUG
Delete all lines NOT containing error (same as :g!)
Delete empty lines
Append text to every matching line

name: v / V / Ctrl-v
description: Select text character-wise, line-wise, or as a rectangular block.

examples.description: Character-wise selection; then d, y, c, >, < act on it
Line-wise selection
Block (column) selection
Insert // at the start of four lines at once
Reselect the last visual selection

notes: In block mode, $ extends to each line end and A appends to every line.

name: "ayy / "+y / :reg
description: Use named registers and the system clipboard.

examples.description: Yank the line into register a ("Ayy appends to it)
Put from register a
Yank to the system clipboard (needs +clipboard support)
Put the last yank, even after a delete overwrote the unnamed register
Show register contents

notes: In Insert mode, Ctrl-r a inserts register a.

name: qa ... q / @a
description: Record a sequence of keystrokes and replay it.

examples.description: Start recording into register a; q stops
Play macro a (@@ replays the last macro)
Run macro a ten times
Run macro a on every line

notes: Start macros with a motion like 0 so they behave the same on each line.

name: ma / 'a / `a
description: Set bookmarks and jump back to them.

examples.description: Set mark a at the cursor (uppercase A works across files)
Jump to the line of mark a
Jump to the exact position of mark a
Jump to the position of the last change
List marks

name: :ls / :bn / :bp / :b
description: List and switch between open buffers (files).

examples.description: List buffers
Next / previous buffer
Switch to buffer 3 (or :b part-of-name with Tab completion)
Close (delete) the current buffer

name: :sp / :vsp / Ctrl-w
description: Split the window and move between splits.

examples.description: Horizontal split (opens file.txt above)
Vertical split of the current file
Move to the split left/down/up/right (Ctrl-w w cycles)
Make all splits equal size
Close the current split (:only closes all others)

name: :tabnew / gt / gT
description: Open and navigate tab pages.

examples.description: Open a file in a new tab
Next / previous tab (2gt goes to tab 2)
Close the current tab

name: :set number / :set paste
description: Change editor options for the current session.

examples.description: Show line numbers (:set relativenumber for relative)
Turn an option off (append ! to toggle: :set number!)
Paste from terminal without auto-indent mangling; :set nopaste afterwards
Use 4 spaces for indentation
Show an option's current value

notes: Put options in ~/.vimrc to make them permanent.
'paste' is unnecessary in Vim 8+ and Neovim with terminals supporting bracketed paste (Neovim marks it obsolete).

name: :!cmd
description: Run a shell command, or filter text through one.

examples.description: Run a shell command and show the output
Run the current file (% expands to the file name)
Insert command output below the cursor
Replace the whole buffer with its output through jq (format JSON)

name: :sort
description: Sort lines in the buffer or a range.

examples.description: Sort all lines
Sort and remove duplicates
Numeric sort
Reverse-sort the visual selection

name: zf / za / zR / zM
description: Fold (collapse) and unfold regions of text.

examples.description: Create a fold over a paragraph (manual foldmethod)
Toggle the fold under the cursor
Open all folds / close all folds
Fold automatically by indentation (or syntax, marker, expr)
